title: Are US Long Bonds A Buy? (Part I)
gist: Gavekal opens a report series asking whether US long bonds now belong in portfolios, pointing to the Treasury's expanded debt buybacks and a recent US foreign-exchange intervention it characterizes as a disguised bond-market intervention.

themes.theme: Treasury Buybacks and Disguised Bond Intervention

insights.claim: The US Treasury has been increasing its buybacks of its own long-term debt, a policy shift significant enough that private investors should take note.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: An expanding Treasury buyback program can act as a technical demand backstop for long-dated bonds, a factor investors should weigh when assessing duration exposure.
insights.quote: The US Treasury is buying back more of its own long-term debt. Perhaps private investors should take note.
insights.locator: The US Treasury is buying back more of its own long-term debt

insights.claim: The US's recent unusual foreign exchange intervention was, in substance, a bond market intervention carried out under the guise of FX policy.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: If FX intervention is really being used to manage the bond market, official rhetoric about currency policy may be masking a more direct effort to cap long-term yields, which investors should track through Treasury and Fed operations rather than currency statements alone.
insights.quote: the US's unusual foreign exchange intervention, which was really a bond market intervention in disguise
insights.locator: the first report in this series focuses on the significance of recent policy changes

themes.theme: Long Bonds as Portfolio Holdings and Equity Hedges

insights.claim: Gavekal is examining whether US long bonds now belong in investor portfolios either as outright long positions or as hedges for equities, with long-duration growth stocks singled out as the equity exposure most relevant to that hedge.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Investors holding long-duration growth equities should watch this series for a framework on whether adding long-bond exposure can offset duration risk in their equity book.
insights.quote: whether US long bonds now belong in portfolios, either as outright long positions or as hedges for equities, especially long-duration growth stocks
insights.locator: The question is whether US long bonds now belong in portfolios

insights.claim: Gavekal frames its evaluation of US long bonds around three specific policy drivers in this first installment: the foreign exchange/bond-market intervention, the Treasury's expanded buyback program, and the role of the Federal Reserve.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Investors should monitor Fed policy signals alongside Treasury buyback volumes as the near-term catalysts this report series treats as decisive for the long-bond thesis.
insights.locator: the first report in this series focuses on the significance of recent policy changes

insights.claim: Gavekal plans forthcoming installments covering rising capital demand from both the public and private sectors, bond valuations, and the usefulness of bonds as a portfolio hedge, indicating a multi-part analytical build toward a full buy/sell call on long bonds.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: The eventual investment conclusion depends on later installments assessing capital demand and valuation, so this Part I is a premise-setting piece rather than an actionable call yet.
insights.quote: Forthcoming installments will then look at increased demand for capital from both the public and private sectors, bond valuations and the usefulness of bonds as a portfolio hedge.
insights.locator: Forthcoming installments will then look at increased demand for capital
